text:
dmitri: quick sync on the RFC follow-up: we need a concrete manifest translation + admission flow for hosted/dedicated/private. i sketched a few gaps in the original doc we should resolve

elaine: appreciate the sketch. top-level constraints i care about: operator intent (what policies can change at runtime), offline safety for private, and minimizing extra roundtrips for hosted

sam: agree. recommendation: keep control-plane policy as the canonical source, but publish signed 'runtime-bundles' that contain: policy.json, signature, version, bundle_ttl. runtime verifies signature and enforces locally when control-plane is unreachable

anya: small ask: the bundle format needs a well-defined diffing model so console can show "what changed" between versions. include a change-set hash and a human changelog string in the bundle metadata

dmitri: good call. also how do we handle partial enforcement mismatch? e.g., control-plane expresses a quota per-minute, runtime batches tokens and reports only aggregated counts. we need an admission_id to make reconciliation deterministic

sam: admission_id solves that. flow: 1) router gets an admission ticket from control-plane (admission_id + allowed_tokens + expires_at) 2) router forwards request with headers: X-Admission-Id, X-Admission-Estimate 3) runtime uses admission_id when charging and includes admission_id in usage reports

elaine: example headers we can standardize: X-Redwood-Admission-Id: <opaque> , X-Redwood-Admission-Origin: router|local, X-Redwood-Policy-Version: v123. clients never see these; SDK layers translate to QuotaError or retry hints

anya: private edge-case: if runtime enforces while offline, it must not issue admission_ids tied to control-plane keys. solution: runtime signs a local admission token using a local key; control-plane accepts those signed tokens if the policy bundle indicates offline-issuance-allowed and includes a local_key_id mapping. we should limit offline admission TTL (e.g., 5s) and cap total offline allowance window (e.g., cumulative 1 hour between reconciles)

dmitri: nice. need to protect against cross-tenant leakage on shared routers: admission ids must be HMAC(router_key, tenant||nonce||ts). router keys rotate; runtime should accept previous key for a grace period to avoid rejects mid-rotation

sam: reconciliation algorithm idea: control-plane stores admission_id -> claimed_usage. runtime periodically POSTs usage reports: [{admission_id, usage_tokens, timestamp}]. control-plane dedupes by admission_id and sums usage. for locally-signed offline tokens, the control-plane verifies the runtime's signed bundle and accepts usage only if within the bundle lifetime and within allowed offline budget

elaine: tests we need: 1) fallback path where router retries to dedicated after hosted denied and ensure only one admission_id is counted (simulate partial success), 2) offline private enforcement that later reconciles and respects offline budget caps, 3) key rotation acceptance window. add property tests for dedupe

anya: telemetry: emit admission_request_latency_ms, admission_cache_hit, admission_origin, offline_reconcile_lag_seconds, and a metric for "offline_budget_remaining" per-tenant so console can surface it

dmitri: UX: SDKs should map both control-plane and runtime 429s to the same QuotaError type. include error details: {code: 429, reason: "quota_exceeded", origin: "controlplane"|"runtime", admission_id: "...", retry_after: 3} so apps can decide retry/backoff strategies

sam: fallback hints from runtime when overloaded are useful. runtime should return structured metadata: {fallback: "target=dedicated" | "model=degraded" | "retry_after": seconds}. router policy chooses next: prefer same-mode fallback first, then cross-mode if tenant permit

elaine: security note: admission_id must be opaque and not leak tenant names. use base64(HMAC) and avoid embedding tenant ids. store a mapping at runtime to translate admission_id -> tenant at enforcement time, not in the token itself

anya: for manifests, propose bundle TTL default 24h and a max offline cumulative allowance 1h (configurable). admission token TTL default 5s. will put these as recommendations in the RFC

dmitri: agree. edge-case: what if a runtime restarts and loses local offline counters? it should persist counters to local disk or a small stable store and ship checkpoints; if lost, control-plane should have a reconciliation policy: assume worst-case or accept up to configured "replay forgiveness" window (e.g., 10s)

sam: include an operator CLI to inspect last bundle age and offline_budget_remaining for private tenants. console should surface a red/yellow/green for bundle freshness

ops-bot: deploy: rtime/v1.19.0 canary rolled to 2 nodes in staging by @sam

elaine: i'll draft a short RFC doc with: bundle schema, admission header spec, reconciliation API, recommended TTLs, telemetry hooks, and tests. will include sample pseudo-code for router and runtime to implement. pinging @dmitri @sam @anya for review

dmitri: thanks — i'll add property tests and a small simulation harness to validate double-count and offline-reconcile invariants

anya: will add console UX mocks for the bundle age + offline budget widget.

elaine: TL;DR: signed runtime bundles + admission ids + short offline windows; normalize client-facing 429s; reconciliation via admission_id dedupe; telemetry + console visibility. RFC PR incoming.
